item.title: Google’s AI‑powered satellite sends first haiku from orbit
item.description:
Google’s AI‑powered satellite sends first haiku from orbit

Google’s AI chip‑equipped satellite transmitted its first response from space – a haiku written by the on‑board Gemma 4 model.

🔍 Overview

  • The satellite is part of Project Suncatcher, an experimental effort that could eventually host AI data centers in space.
  • It was launched into orbit earlier this month.
  • After successfully booting its Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), the system generated a space‑themed haiku and sent it back to Earth.

🛰️ Test details

  • Google’s blog post on Friday confirmed that the TPUs were powered up and the Gemma 4 model responded to a prompt for a haiku about being in space.

  • The haiku received on the ground reads:

    Blue marble below
    Data streams in silent grace
    Starlight feeds my core. ✨

  • Google also ran other space‑themed limericks and telemetry prompts during the test.

⚙️ Technical specifics

  • The satellite hosts AI‑optimized TPUs that execute workloads in orbit.
  • The first successful transmission demonstrates that TPUs can operate under space conditions, a prerequisite for future on‑orbit AI services.

🚀 Next steps

  • Google plans a series of tests to evaluate TPU performance under thermal stress and radiation exposure in orbit.
  • Verifying reliable TPU execution is aimed at enabling a twin interconnected satellite architecture slated for 2027.

💡 Why it matters

  • Proving that AI workloads can run on hardware in space opens the possibility of satellite‑based AI data centers.
  • Such capability could reduce latency for Earth‑bound services and enable new types of on‑orbit processing.

#Google #AI #Satellites #TPU #ProjectSuncatcher

Source: Google’s satellite AI server transmits its first response to Earth

item.title: TorchTPU Brings Native PyTorch Support to Google Cloud TPUs
item.description:
TorchTPU Brings Native PyTorch Support to Google Cloud TPUs

With TorchTPU, a native PyTorch backend, TPU is now just another device. The integration lets Transformers, Diffusers and custom kernels run natively on Google’s Tensor Processing Units (TPUs).

🔍 Overview

  • TPU stands for Tensor Processing Unit and is Google’s own AI accelerator.\
  • Google has been designing TPUs for about ten years and uses them for its models, including Gemini.\
  • TPUs are available on Google Cloud, from a single chip up to pods of thousands of chips.

🧩 How it works

  • TorchTPU adds TPU as a new backend to PyTorch.\
  • It includes Pallas kernels tuned for TPUs, support for distributed training, and a torch.compile integration for extra speed.\
  • TPU kernels are written in Pallas, giving low‑level hardware control.\
  • Additional kernels can be imported from the Tokamax library.\
  • Installation on a TPU VM is a single command: 
    1

    pip install torch-tpu --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
  • To load a model on a TPU, set device_map="tpu".\
  • The TensorParallelConfig can be passed to from_pretrained to shard the model across chips, so the full model never has to fit in one place.

⚙️ Key details

  • Transformers v5 is built to be the source of truth for model definitions, enabling them to run anywhere, including TPUs.\
  • Diffusers now treats TPU as a first‑class device.\
  • Example runs on a Cloud TPU v6e‑4 with 4 chips (TP=4), bf16 precision, batch size 1.\
  • At batch size 64, decoding is 21.5× faster on Qwen3‑30B‑A3B and 12.8× faster on Gemma 4 26B‑A4B.\
  • Decode throughput comparisons on a TPU v6e‑8 show Hub kernels outperforming the default implementation.

🚀 Availability

  • The Kernels Hub provides ready‑to‑use TPU kernels.\
  • TorchTPU is publicly installable via pip.\
  • A nightly CI on TPU is being added, with results to appear in the Transformers dashboard.

💡 Why it matters

  • By making TPU a first‑class device in PyTorch, developers can train and serve large language models on Google Cloud without rewriting code.\
  • Sharding with TensorParallelConfig removes the need for a single device to hold the entire model, enabling very large models to run on TPU pods.

Component Summary

Component Role
TorchTPU Adds TPU as a PyTorch backend
Pallas kernels Tuned TPU kernels, low‑level control
Tokamax library Additional kernels that can be imported

#PyTorch #TPU #TorchTPU #Transformers #Diffusers

Source: Hugging Face ❤️ TorchTPU: TPUs, Natively

item.title: Google to Launch AI Processor Satellite via Project Suncatcher
item.description:
Google to Launch AI Processor Satellite via Project Suncatcher

Google is launching a satellite equipped with its AI processors on October 1st to test their performance in space. This mission is part of Project Suncatcher, an experimental initiative that could eventually put AI data centers into orbit.

⚙️ Key details

  • Launch Date: October 1st
  • Launch Vehicle: SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket
  • Hardware: Google’s Tensor Processing Units (TPUs)
  • Orbit: Low Earth orbit, where the satellite will harness the power of the sun

🔍 Overview

The goal of the mission is to measure how well TPUs “handle the physical stress of spaceflight and the radiation and thermal extremes of space.” While Google found during testing that its TPUs can withstand radiation and high levels of g-force, the company notes that “some things can only be tested in space.”

🧩 How it works

Google is testing a cooling system using radiators and heat pipes while the chips are in orbit. According to Travis Beals, Project Suncatcher’s senior director of product management, the chips can only run for approximately 15 minutes before they must be turned off to cool down.

🚀 Availability

Following this initial launch, Google plans to put two satellites into orbit next year.

#Google #ProjectSuncatcher #TPU #SpaceX #SpaceAI

Source: Google is sending an AI satellite into space next week
